classification.difficultyReason: Find the triangle's remaining angle and connect it to the tangent–chord angle using the alternate segment theorem.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Circle tangent to a horizontal line at its bottom point. A chord from the upper-left vertex through the right-hand circumference vertex extends to the external point on the tangent. Preserve the larger 100° angle from the right-directed tangent to the upper-left chord, with the smaller x angle nested inside it.
spec.mathematics: The external angle is 36°. The upper-left angle of the triangle formed by the upper-left vertex, tangent contact and external point is 44°. The alternate segment theorem equates that angle to x. Construction coordinates enforce the circle incidences, tangency and collinearity; coordinate names are not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 100°, 36° and x are visible in the question figure. The supplied 44° answer is excluded.

answer.worked:
The angle at the upper-left vertex is
$$\begin{aligned}
180^\circ-100^\circ-36^\circ&=44^\circ.
\end{aligned}$$
By the alternate segment theorem,
$$x=44^\circ.$$
